title: BioLab independent visual QA issue ledger
sourceChecks: All 259 Biology SVG bytes fetched and checked for root/viewBox, embedded script/onload; all 40 topic asset references cross-checked for existence and alt text. No findings from these narrow checks.
verificationLimits: Science defects are independently inferred from inspected original SVG source. Full-site Chromium at six widths and screenshot evidence were not executed; screenshotEvidence is null. This is NOT scientific certification.

issues.sourceEvidence: SVG paths M155 205 V267; M150 327 V377 H33 V175 H59; M252 298 H329 V175 H253, and all strokes lack marker-end.
issues.defect: Fish circulation has an unlabeled/missing body-tissue stage and ambiguous paths. A line runs from the gill area around the bottom back toward the heart; no flow arrowheads are defined. Mammalian diagram adds directionless parallel paths.
issues.educationalImpact: May teach that fish blood can return directly from gills to heart rather than passing through systemic capillaries first.
issues.expectedStructure: Fish: heart → gill capillaries → systemic capillaries → heart, one continuous circulation. Mammal: right heart → lungs → left heart → body → right heart, two unambiguous ordered circuits.
issues.recommendedChange: Replace with discrete gill, body, heart nodes and one-way clearly arrowheaded connectors; validate one continuous fish circuit and two mammalian circuits against B3.2.

issues.browserVerification: pending; no screenshot exists at this SHA

issues.sourceEvidence: D3.1 lesson assets: d31-cycle-feedback, d31-fertilization-sequence, d31-flower-structures. Do not treat handout D3.2 as current syllabus code.
issues.defect: No dedicated registered male or female reproductive-system anatomy figure exists in D3.1; only cycle, fertilization and flower assets are registered.
issues.educationalImpact: Students have no internal structural reference for ovary/oviduct/uterus/cervix/vagina or vas deferens/testis/epididymis/urethra during relevant teaching.
issues.expectedStructure: Where anatomical diagrams are needed, show typical female and male systems with correctly oriented ducts, distinct routes, and structure names; distinguish typical anatomical variation.
issues.recommendedChange: Commission original figures with clinically and biologically correct pathways; attach only to relevant understandings, not as generic decoration.

issues.sourceEvidence: Rectangular chamber elements at x226–526 and x672–972; labels 'Pulmonary valve' at x27,525 and 'Aortic valve' at x986,473; no visible cusps.
issues.defect: Diagram calls itself a frontal heart and names pulmonary/aortic/tricuspid/mitral valves, but its organs are detached rectangles; the semilunar valve labels do not indicate visible valve leaflets.
issues.educationalImpact: Functional blood flow is broadly sound, but students may wrongly use this as a heart-anatomy drawing model or fail to locate valve structures.
issues.expectedStructure: Two atria, two ventricular chambers with correct relative wall thickness, septum, four visibly distinct valves and connected great vessels with unambiguous arrows.
issues.recommendedChange: Either retitle as flow-topology chart and add a separate anatomical frontal diagram, or replace with anatomical plan showing valves at correct outflow/atrioventricular junctions.

issues.sourceEvidence: Only visible explanatory labels: 'Bundles in a peripheral ring' and 'Central xylem; phloem between arms'.
issues.defect: Stem/root tissue cross-sections show colored bundles but do not identify xylem versus phloem with direct leaders; epidermis, cortex, and stem pith are not explicitly labeled.
issues.educationalImpact: Students may memorize general ring/star shapes yet fail to map named tissues in an observation-plan drawing.
issues.expectedStructure: Stem: bundles arranged in ring, xylem inward and phloem outward, epidermis/cortex/pith as appropriate. Root: central star xylem, phloem between arms and outer tissue layers.
issues.recommendedChange: Keep geometric arrangements but add tissue-specific leaders or a small matched key; verify each colored tissue against an authentic micrograph.

issues.defect: Named tissue labels appear in a right-side list without leaders; at narrow sizes, the diagram is likely too small for reliable association with the correct tissue layer.

issues.sourceEvidence: Four identical vertical <line> elements at x230,380,530,680 from y135 to290 with identical dasharray 7 8.
issues.defect: One unbroken dashed vertical line connects each A–T and G–C pair. If interpreted as hydrogen bonds, this implies equal single dashed contacts rather than the 2 A–T and 3 G–C pattern.
issues.educationalImpact: Could obscure the reason complementary base-pair strengths differ and fail the handout's DNA model convention.
issues.expectedStructure: A–T pairs represented by two hydrogen-bond contacts and G–C by three; antiparallel strands remain correctly oriented 5′/3′.
issues.recommendedChange: Depict two/three short dashed contacts respectively, or explicitly label existing dashes as generic pair alignment rather than bond counts.

issues.sourceEvidence: SVG reactant text 'Amino acid 1 + amino acid 2'; product H2N–CH(R1)–C(=O)–NH–CH(R2)–COOH + H2O.
issues.defect: Condensation reaction names 'amino acid 1 + amino acid 2' but shows only the generalized product formula; the OH and H lost from reactants are not drawn.
issues.educationalImpact: Does not itself teach how the covalent peptide linkage forms, despite being used as a bonding process diagram.
issues.expectedStructure: Two complete generalized amino acid reactants showing -COOH and -NH2, a water product and -C(=O)-NH- in the dipeptide; chemically valid carbon and nitrogen valences.
issues.recommendedChange: Keep the correct product formula; add a separate explicit reaction inset, or retitle the figure as a peptide-bond product summary.
